entities.summary: Hugo Dyonizy Steinhaus was a Polish mathematician and educator. Steinhaus obtained his PhD under David Hilbert at Göttingen University in 1911 and later became a professor at the Jan Kazimierz University in Lwów, where he helped establish what later became known as the Lwów School of Mathematics. He is credited with "discovering" mathematician Stefan Banach, with whom he gave a notable contribution to functional analysis through the Banach–Steinhaus theorem. After World War II Steinhaus played an important part in the establishment of the mathematics department at Wrocław University and in the revival of Polish mathematics from the destruction of the war.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hugo Steinhaus played a crucial role in the revival of Polish mathematics after World War II and made significant contributions to functional analysis through his work with Stefan Banach. His establishment of the Lwów School of Mathematics helped shape the development of modern mathematics.
